questions.scenarioContext: A patient remains at home for a scheduled follow-up while the clinician remains at the clinic. They speak and see each other through a live, two-way video connection, with questions answered during the same encounter.
questions.prompt: Which service format best describes this visit?

choices.A: An asynchronous exchange of stored portal messages.
choices.B: A home health visit with a clinician physically present in the residence.
choices.C: A synchronous telehealth visit using real-time audio and video.
choices.D: An in-person outpatient visit at a fixed clinic location.

questions.explanation: Synchronous telehealth involves real-time interaction between participants in different locations. A portal message reviewed later is asynchronous, and neither a home visit nor an in-person clinic visit matches the locations described.

questions.scenarioContext: An adult has a verified order for furosemide 60 mg orally once daily. The former solution contained 10 mg/mL, and an old worksheet listed 6 mL per dose. The pharmacy now supplies a solution containing 8 mg/mL and has confirmed that the prescribed milligram dose remains unchanged. A trained medical assistant is authorized to prepare the dose under applicable law and clinic policy.
questions.prompt: What volume should the updated worksheet show for the current solution? Round to the nearest 0.1 mL.

choices.A: 7.5 mL
choices.B: 6 mL
choices.C: 4.8 mL
choices.D: 12 mL

questions.explanation: Use the current concentration: 60 mg / 8 mg/mL = 7.5 mL. Reusing the old 6 mL volume would provide 48 mg from the new solution, rather than the ordered 60 mg. A concentration change requires recalculating volume even when the prescribed milligram dose stays the same.

questions.prompt: When combining gastr/o with -scopy and with -itis, which pair follows the usual combining-vowel rule?

choices.A: Gastroscopy and gastroitis.
choices.B: Gastroscopy and gastritis.
choices.C: Gastrscopy and gastritis.
choices.D: Gastrscopy and gastroitis.

questions.explanation: The combining vowel is retained before the consonant-starting suffix -scopy, producing gastroscopy. It is usually dropped before a vowel-starting suffix such as -itis, producing gastritis.

questions.scenarioContext: During a wellness visit, a 9-year-old proudly describes learning new school skills and keeping a record of tasks mastered through practice. The child is especially pleased when an adult recognizes the improvement.
questions.prompt: In Erikson's framework, which developmental task is most directly reflected in this emphasis on mastering skills?

choices.A: Developing basic trust in a dependable caregiver.
choices.B: Developing ego integrity through acceptance of a life history.
choices.C: Developing intimate partnerships during early adulthood.
choices.D: Developing industry through a growing sense of competence.

questions.explanation: Industry versus inferiority is associated with developing competence through learning, practice, and accomplishment during the school-age years. The child's focus on mastering tasks fits industry, rather than the infancy, early-adult, or later-adult tasks in the other choices.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient asks whether a single-ingredient acetaminophen pain reliever can be used with a differently branded nighttime pain product. The second product's Drug Facts label lists both acetaminophen and diphenhydramine. The clinician has not reviewed the proposed combination.
questions.prompt: Which finding is most important to identify when flagging the combination for review?

choices.A: The shared acetaminophen ingredient creates a risk of unintentional duplicate dosing.
choices.B: The different brand names establish separate acetaminophen exposure limits for the two products.
choices.C: The nonprescription status makes ingredient overlap less relevant than the product names.
choices.D: Taking the products at different clock times removes concern about total acetaminophen intake.

questions.explanation: Both products supply acetaminophen, so using them together can unintentionally increase total exposure and the risk of harm. Active ingredients, not brand names or marketing categories, determine this duplication; the patient needs clinician or pharmacist review before adding the second product.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient with hand arthritis has difficulty fastening clothing and using eating utensils. The clinician requests an evaluation of adaptive equipment and methods for performing these daily activities, rather than a new diet or a gait-training program.
questions.prompt: Which professional has the most directly relevant expertise for this referral?

choices.A: A registered dietitian.
choices.B: A physical therapist.
choices.C: An occupational therapist.
choices.D: A respiratory therapist.

questions.explanation: Occupational therapists help people perform daily activities and can recommend adaptive equipment for tasks such as dressing and eating. A physical therapist may address movement and mobility, but adapting the specified daily tasks is the central referral need.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient's existing nutrition plan calls for a snack with at least 10 g of protein and no more than 3 g of saturated fat. The patient brings four single-serving snack labels and plans to eat one full serving.
questions.prompt: Which label meets both requirements of the supplied plan?

choices.A: Protein 15 g; saturated fat 5 g.
choices.B: Protein 12 g; saturated fat 2 g.
choices.C: Protein 8 g; saturated fat 1 g.
choices.D: Protein 6 g; saturated fat 4 g.

questions.explanation: The snack with 12 g of protein and 2 g of saturated fat meets both the minimum protein amount and maximum saturated-fat amount. The 15 g protein snack exceeds the fat limit; the other two snacks do not reach the protein minimum.

questions.scenarioContext: A note describes a skin lesion on the dorsal surface of the left hand. Before showing the area to the provider, the assistant needs to distinguish this surface from the palm.
questions.prompt: Which area does dorsal identify in this note?

choices.A: The palm of the left hand.
choices.B: The back of the left hand, opposite the palm.
choices.C: The surface between the left thumb and index finger.
choices.D: The back of the right hand, opposite its palm.

questions.explanation: The dorsal surface of the hand is its back, opposite the palmar surface. The left-hand laterality remains unchanged; dorsal does not identify the web space between the thumb and index finger.

questions.scenarioContext: A medication reference explains that oral enalapril is a prodrug and is chemically converted in the body to enalaprilat, its active form. A patient asks why the reference uses two related names for the medicine and its active product.
questions.prompt: Which pharmacokinetic process describes this conversion to an active form?

choices.A: Absorption of unchanged medicine into the bloodstream.
choices.B: Distribution of unchanged medicine from blood into tissues.
choices.C: Excretion of unchanged medicine from the body.
choices.D: Metabolism that transforms a prodrug into an active metabolite.

questions.explanation: Metabolism chemically transforms a drug and can produce an active metabolite, as the supplied reference describes for enalapril. Absorption and distribution move a drug between locations, while excretion removes drug or metabolites; these processes do not themselves describe the stated chemical conversion.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes suppression from repression?

choices.A: Suppression consciously sets aside a distressing thought; repression excludes it from awareness unconsciously.
choices.B: Suppression excludes a thought unconsciously; repression consciously sets it aside for later consideration.
choices.C: Suppression redirects emotion to another target; repression channels an impulse into a socially acceptable activity.
choices.D: Suppression attributes a feeling to another person; repression supplies an acceptable justification for behavior.

questions.explanation: Suppression is a conscious decision to set a distressing thought aside, often to address it later. Repression involves unconscious exclusion from awareness; the other descriptions confuse these concepts with different defense mechanisms.

questions.scenarioContext: Several independent physician practices, a hospital, and other health professionals form a joint organization. They coordinate services for a defined patient population and accept shared accountability for the quality and total cost of that population's care.
questions.prompt: Which organizational model best matches this description?

choices.A: A single-practice patient-centered medical home focused on its own primary care team.
choices.B: A retail pharmacy organized around dispensing individual prescriptions.
choices.C: An accountable care organization linking participating providers across settings.
choices.D: A freestanding diagnostic laboratory organized around specimen testing.

questions.explanation: An accountable care organization brings participating clinicians and other providers together around coordinated care and accountability for a population's quality and cost. A primary care medical home emphasizes the organization of a primary care practice, while the described arrangement spans multiple participating organizations.

questions.scenarioContext: Clinic policy requires medication-stock cabinets to be locked outside authorized access and their keys returned to a designated secure key locker after each use. A staff member locks a cabinet but leaves its key in an unlocked desk drawer nearby.
questions.prompt: Which action completes the required storage-security process?

choices.A: Leave the key in the drawer and label the drawer for staff use.
choices.B: Hang the key behind the desk so it is out of direct patient view.
choices.C: Put the key back in the cabinet lock so the next authorized staff member can find it.
choices.D: Return the key to the designated secure key locker as the policy requires.

questions.explanation: Locking the stock cabinet is only one part of the supplied policy; its key must also be secured in the designated location. A key left in an unlocked drawer, on a hook, or in the lock can undermine access control, even if it is not immediately visible.

questions.scenarioContext: A verified prescription says to take one capsule by mouth every other day. A draft instruction substitutes QOD. The clinic's documentation policy prohibits QD and QOD because they can be confused and requires the frequency to be written in full.
questions.prompt: Which instruction preserves the verified frequency and follows the policy?

choices.A: Take one capsule by mouth every other day.
choices.B: Take one capsule by mouth once daily.
choices.C: Take one capsule by mouth twice daily.
choices.D: Take one capsule by mouth every other week.

questions.explanation: Writing every other day in full retains the verified schedule and avoids the prohibited abbreviation. Once daily would increase dosing frequency, while twice daily and every other week would also change the prescribed regimen.

questions.scenarioContext: A clinician's plan includes topical hydrocortisone cream for a small skin rash and a transdermal nicotine patch for smoking cessation. A patient asks why two products applied to skin can have different intended treatment targets.
questions.prompt: Which explanation best distinguishes their intended delivery?

choices.A: Both are intended primarily for local skin effects; the dosage-form names mainly describe packaging.
choices.B: The cream is intended primarily for a local skin effect, while the patch delivers medicine through skin for systemic action.
choices.C: The cream is intended for systemic delivery, while the patch is intended to act at its application site.
choices.D: The intended effect depends primarily on the amount placed on skin rather than the formulation and delivery system.

questions.explanation: A transdermal nicotine patch is designed to deliver medicine across the skin for systemic effects, whereas the hydrocortisone cream in this plan targets local skin inflammation. Local intent does not mean that systemic absorption of a topical product is impossible; the distinction concerns the formulation's intended delivery and effect.

questions.scenarioContext: A nationally certified medical assistant moves to a clinic in another state and is asked to perform a task not previously included in the assistant's duties. The clinic's onboarding policy requires review of applicable state permissions, any required governmental credential, task training, and supervision before a new task is assigned. The assistant believes national certification makes that review unnecessary.
questions.prompt: Which conclusion best addresses this belief about certification and legal practice authority?

choices.A: Permission for the task in the former workplace establishes permission in the new state.
choices.B: A clinician's request makes the national certificate sufficient without reviewing the task requirements.
choices.C: A national examination makes authorized duties identical wherever the credential is recognized.
choices.D: Certification recognizes qualifications; permission for the new task still requires the specified legal, training, and supervision review.

questions.explanation: National certification recognizes qualifications but does not by itself establish identical legal authority for every task in every jurisdiction. The supplied policy requires a separate review before assigning the new task, including any license or other governmental credential required for that role and location.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient grieving a family member's death describes laughing over a happy memory one morning and feeling tearful later that day. The patient continues basic daily activities and worries that moving between emotions means grieving incorrectly.
questions.prompt: Which interpretation is most appropriate for the assistant to reinforce?

choices.A: Renewed sadness after a pleasant memory suggests a return to the beginning of a fixed grief sequence.
choices.B: Laughing while remembering the deceased suggests the loss is no longer emotionally significant.
choices.C: Sadness and positive memories can occur at different times without following a fixed progression.
choices.D: Alternating feelings are sufficient to classify the response as a complicated grief disorder.

questions.explanation: Grief responses can vary and recur, and people do not necessarily move through emotions in a fixed sequence. A pleasant memory followed by sadness does not by itself establish incorrect grieving or a disorder; the assistant can acknowledge the experience without assigning a stage or diagnosis.

questions.scenarioContext: During a dietary history, a patient reports following a vegan diet with no animal-derived foods, no vitamin B12-fortified foods, and no supplements. The patient regularly eats fruits, vegetables, beans, and whole grains and asks whether this pattern supplies every needed vitamin.
questions.prompt: Which nutrient-source concern is most appropriate to bring to the clinician or dietitian?

choices.A: Vitamin C may require an animal-derived source despite the regular fruit and vegetable intake.
choices.B: Vitamin B12 needs a reliable source, such as fortified foods or supplementation reviewed with the care team.
choices.C: Dietary fiber may require a supplement because beans and whole grains do not provide it.
choices.D: Vitamin K cannot be obtained from plant foods and therefore requires an animal-derived source.

questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 is naturally found primarily in animal-derived foods, and reliable fortified foods or supplements are important sources for people who exclude those foods. The reported absence of both fortified sources and supplementation warrants review; the assistant should not diagnose deficiency or independently prescribe a supplement dose.

questions.scenarioContext: An authorized, trained medical assistant gives a correctly ordered oral medication at 10:20 a.m. but accidentally records the administration time as 10:02 a.m. Clinic policy requires dated and timed corrections that retain the original entry and audit trail. No second dose was given.
questions.prompt: Which action best fulfills the right of accurate medication documentation?

choices.A: Make a dated and timed correction identifying 10:20 a.m. as the actual administration time while preserving the original entry.
choices.B: Delete the original administration entry and replace it without retaining a correction history.
choices.C: Leave the recorded time unchanged and tell the next assistant about the error verbally.
choices.D: Enter a second administration at 10:20 a.m. so that one of the two entries has the correct time.

questions.explanation: Accurate medication documentation should reflect the actual administration, and the supplied policy requires a traceable correction. Adding another administration would falsely imply a second dose, while deleting the history or relying only on a verbal explanation would not provide the required accurate, auditable record.

questions.scenarioContext: During a routine visit, a patient practices a provider-recommended breathing exercise and asks whether the diaphragm relaxes to pull air into the lungs. The medical assistant uses an approved diagram to explain normal quiet inhalation.
questions.prompt: Which description correctly explains the diaphragm's role during inhalation?

choices.A: It contracts and moves downward, increasing the volume of the chest cavity.
choices.B: It relaxes and moves upward, increasing the volume of the chest cavity.
choices.C: It contracts and moves upward, decreasing the volume of the chest cavity.
choices.D: It relaxes and moves downward, decreasing the volume of the chest cavity.

questions.explanation: During quiet inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and moves downward, increasing thoracic volume. The resulting pressure change allows air to flow into the lungs. Relaxation and upward movement of the diaphragm normally contribute to quiet exhalation, linking skeletal muscle function with ventilation.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient with provider-confirmed obstructive sleep apnea is reviewing the sleep-study summary. The patient asks why the report uses the word "obstructive" when describing the nighttime pauses in airflow. The medical assistant reinforces the provider's explanation.
questions.prompt: Which mechanism is characteristic of obstructive sleep apnea?

choices.A: The brain intermittently stops sending the signals needed to initiate breathing.
choices.B: The lower airways repeatedly narrow because of allergic inflammation in the lungs.
choices.C: Upper-airway tissues narrow or block the passage of air during sleep.
choices.D: Fluid in the pleural space prevents the lungs from expanding during sleep.

questions.explanation: Obstructive sleep apnea involves repeated narrowing or blockage of the upper airway during sleep. Problems with the brain's respiratory signals characterize central sleep apnea, a different mechanism. Lower-airway allergic narrowing and pleural fluid do not describe the obstructive process documented here.

questions.scenarioContext: A child returns after a throat infection. The provider documents reactive cervical lymph nodes and explains that these structures participate in the local immune response. The parent asks whether these nodes mainly filter the blood.
questions.prompt: Which description correctly states the normal role of these lymph nodes?

choices.A: They filter circulating blood and remove aging red blood cells.
choices.B: They produce digestive enzymes that enter the upper throat.
choices.C: They produce the hormones that regulate the body's metabolic rate.
choices.D: They filter lymph and contain immune cells that respond to foreign material.

questions.explanation: Lymph nodes filter lymph and contain immune cells, including lymphocytes, that help respond to infection and other foreign material. They are different from the spleen, which filters blood and removes aging red blood cells. The existing provider assessment explains the context; the assistant is not determining the cause of an enlarged node.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient with provider-diagnosed acute viral hepatitis has yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes. The provider has explained that impaired liver processing is allowing a pigment to accumulate. The medical assistant reinforces this explanation.
questions.prompt: Which substance is responsible for this yellow discoloration?

choices.A: Hemoglobin
choices.B: Bilirubin
choices.C: Melanin
choices.D: Keratin

questions.explanation: Bilirubin is a yellowish substance produced during the breakdown of old red blood cells and normally processed and eliminated by the liver. Accumulation can cause jaundice, including yellowing of the skin and sclerae. Melanin contributes to normal skin pigmentation but is not the pigment responsible for jaundice.

questions.prompt: Which anatomical plane divides the body into right and left portions without necessarily creating equal halves?

choices.A: Sagittal plane
choices.B: Coronal plane
choices.C: Transverse plane
choices.D: Oblique plane

questions.explanation: A sagittal plane divides the body into right and left portions. A midsagittal plane is the specific sagittal plane that creates equal right and left halves. A coronal plane separates anterior from posterior portions, while a transverse plane separates superior from inferior portions.

questions.scenarioContext: At a scheduled follow-up, a patient with right-sided heart failure has stable bilateral ankle edema that the provider attributes to the heart condition. The patient asks how a problem in the chest can cause swelling in the legs. The medical assistant reinforces the documented explanation.
questions.prompt: Which mechanism best connects the impaired right-heart pumping with this edema?

choices.A: Reduced liver albumin production lowers the force retaining water within blood vessels.
choices.B: Inflammation in the ankle joints increases local tissue swelling around the joint capsule.
choices.C: Obstruction of leg lymphatic vessels prevents removal of interstitial fluid.
choices.D: Blood backs up in systemic veins, promoting movement of fluid into surrounding tissues.

questions.explanation: Impaired right-heart pumping can cause blood to back up in the systemic venous circulation. Increased vascular pressure promotes movement of fluid into surrounding tissues, producing peripheral edema. Low albumin, local inflammation, and lymphatic obstruction can also cause swelling, but they do not describe the right-heart mechanism specified in this record.

questions.prompt: Which normal function is performed by platelets during the initial response to a small blood vessel injury?

choices.A: Transporting oxygen from the lungs to injured tissues.
choices.B: Engulfing bacteria that enter through the injured surface.
choices.C: Adhering at the damaged site and aggregating to form an initial plug.
choices.D: Maintaining plasma oncotic pressure to retain water in blood vessels.

questions.explanation: Platelets adhere to a damaged vessel and aggregate to help form the initial platelet plug. Clotting factors subsequently help stabilize the plug with fibrin. Red blood cells carry oxygen, certain white blood cells engulf pathogens, and plasma proteins such as albumin help maintain oncotic pressure.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient is being evaluated by the provider for possible gout. The provider explains that an elevated serum urate result alone does not establish the diagnosis and has ordered collection of fluid from the affected joint. The patient asks what the fluid can show that supports gout.
questions.prompt: Which purpose of examining the joint fluid is most specific to this evaluation?

choices.A: Culturing the joint fluid to identify bacterial growth.
choices.B: Looking for monosodium urate crystals within the joint fluid.
choices.C: Counting white blood cells to identify inflammation in the joint fluid.
choices.D: Looking for blood in the joint fluid to identify a possible joint bleed.

questions.explanation: Monosodium urate crystals in fluid from an affected joint support a diagnosis of gout. An elevated serum urate level alone does not prove gout because some people have high urate without the disease. An elevated joint-fluid white blood cell count indicates inflammation but is not specific for gout, while culture checks for infection.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient with provider-documented mitral valve regurgitation is reviewing a heart diagram during follow-up. The provider has described the valve as not closing tightly. The medical assistant reinforces the valve's normal function.
questions.prompt: Which normal function is reduced when a heart valve does not seal properly?

choices.A: Generating the electrical impulse that starts each heartbeat.
choices.B: Maintaining one-way blood flow by preventing backward leakage.
choices.C: Adding oxygen to blood before it enters the left ventricle.
choices.D: Filtering metabolic wastes from blood before it enters the aorta.

questions.explanation: Heart valves help maintain one-way blood flow by opening to allow forward movement and closing to prevent backflow. A valve that does not close tightly can allow regurgitation, or backward leakage. Generating the heartbeat's initiating impulse is a function of the cardiac conduction system rather than the valve.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient attends an outpatient follow-up after hospitalization for a provider-diagnosed ischemic stroke. The patient says, "I thought every stroke meant that a blood vessel burst." The medical assistant reinforces the discharge explanation about stroke types.
questions.prompt: Which process describes an ischemic stroke?

choices.A: An arterial blockage reduces blood flow and oxygen delivery to part of the brain.
choices.B: A ruptured cerebral blood vessel releases blood into or around brain tissue.
choices.C: Abnormal electrical activity spreads through brain cells and produces a seizure.
choices.D: Degeneration of peripheral sensory nerves reduces sensation in the feet.

questions.explanation: An ischemic stroke results from blocked blood flow that deprives part of the brain of oxygen and nutrients. A hemorrhagic stroke results from bleeding into or around the brain after a vessel ruptures. The question concerns an established diagnosis and does not ask the assistant to distinguish stroke types in a patient with new symptoms.

questions.scenarioContext: A blood pressure cuff has an artery marker that its instructions require aligning with the brachial artery. The marker is currently facing the back of the upper arm rather than the specified anterior-medial position.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant correct?

choices.A: Leave the marker at the back and increase cuff inflation pressure.
choices.B: Place the stethoscope over the marker at the back regardless of artery location.
choices.C: Rotate and reapply the cuff so the marker aligns with the specified artery position.
choices.D: Use the cuff upside down without checking the remaining placement instructions.

questions.explanation: The marker should follow the cuff's specified artery alignment. Increasing pressure or moving the stethoscope to an incorrect anatomical location does not correct cuff orientation.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter is being assisted into a wheelchair. The assistant is trained and authorized for the routine bag-positioning task. Clinic procedure keeps the closed drainage system intact, the bag below the bladder, and the bag off the floor. The bag is currently on the patient's lap.
questions.prompt: Which preparation follows the procedure?

choices.A: Disconnect the tubing temporarily so the bag is easier to carry.
choices.B: Leave the bag on the lap above bladder level during the trip.
choices.C: Set the bag on the floor so it is well below the bladder.
choices.D: Secure the bag in its appropriate holder below bladder level without disconnecting the system.

questions.explanation: The stated placement and closed-system requirements apply during transfer as well as at rest. A lap position, floor placement, or unneeded disconnection does not meet those conditions.

questions.scenarioContext: After an examination in lithotomy, clinic technique calls for coordinated support of both legs while lowering them from the stirrups. A second trained helper is present.
questions.prompt: How should the assistants help the patient reposition?

choices.A: Ask the patient to twist onto the side before either leg is supported.
choices.B: Drop one stirrup while leaving the other leg unsupported.
choices.C: Coordinate support and lowering of both legs using the prescribed technique.
choices.D: Pull the patient toward the end of the table with both feet still fixed.

questions.explanation: Coordinated support follows the stated technique and avoids uncontrolled asymmetric movement. The presence of the second helper permits the planned repositioning rather than improvisation.

questions.scenarioContext: A wall-mounted liquid-soap dispenser is partly empty. A coworker proposes pouring fresh soap into the remaining soap to fill it. The dispenser has a manufacturer-approved replacement and cleaning procedure.
questions.prompt: Which action is appropriate?

choices.A: Add fresh soap directly to the remaining soap without processing the dispenser.
choices.B: Mix different soaps in the dispenser to strengthen their effect.
choices.C: Add water to the remaining soap to restore the full level.
choices.D: Follow the approved dispenser procedure rather than topping off the partly filled soap.

questions.explanation: Topping off liquid soap can introduce or support contamination. The approved dispenser replacement and cleaning process is preferable to adding soap or water to the residual contents.

questions.scenarioContext: A sterile-field procedure defines the outer 1-inch border of the wrapper as nonsterile. A sterile forceps has been placed entirely on that border rather than in the sterile central area.
questions.prompt: How should the forceps be handled?

choices.A: Treat it as contaminated and obtain a sterile replacement.
choices.B: Move it from the border to the center and consider it sterile again.
choices.C: Ask the patient whether it appears clean before deciding.
choices.D: Use it if only the handle lies within the border.

questions.explanation: The supplied field boundary means the instrument contacted a nonsterile area. Moving it afterward or judging its appearance does not restore sterility.

questions.scenarioContext: A reusable instrument must be sterile because it enters sterile tissue. Its manufacturer prohibits steam and validates a specific low-temperature sterilization method. The clinic has only a steam unit but can arrange the validated method through its approved processing service.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant arrange?

choices.A: Substitute high-level disinfection for the required validated sterilization.
choices.B: Use the clinic steam cycle despite the manufacturer's prohibition.
choices.C: Choose an unvalidated cooler steam cycle without obtaining an approved process.
choices.D: The validated compatible sterilization process through the approved service before use.

questions.explanation: The device must meet both the sterility requirement and material compatibility instructions. An available but prohibited cycle or a lower processing level is not an equivalent substitute.

questions.scenarioContext: A qualified clinician is administering an IV infusion in a patient's left arm. A venous specimen is ordered, and clinic collection procedure directs a suitable opposite-arm site when available. The assistant is not authorized to stop or adjust the infusion. A suitable right-arm site is available.
questions.prompt: Which approach follows this procedure?

choices.A: Collect from the infusion tubing without the required authorization.
choices.B: Collect from the suitable right arm without independently changing the infusion.
choices.C: Stop the infusion independently and collect above its insertion site.
choices.D: Collect from the left infusion site and relabel the specimen as right-arm blood.

questions.explanation: The available opposite-arm site follows the stated specimen-collection procedure. This task does not authorize the assistant to manipulate an IV infusion or independently collect from its tubing.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: A specified CLIA-waived test uses a new control lot with an acceptance range of 100-120 units. An old lot's sheet lists 80-100 units. Today's new-lot control result is 90 units. Instructions require the current lot's range and acceptable QC before patient testing.
questions.prompt: Which evaluation is appropriate?

choices.A: Release patient results before verifying the new-lot control range.
choices.B: Accept 90 using the obsolete 80-100 range sheet.
choices.C: QC fails against the current 100-120 range; hold testing and follow corrective instructions.
choices.D: Use whichever lot's range produces a passing value today.

questions.explanation: The acceptance range must match the control lot actually used. Ninety is below the new lot's lower limit of 100 even though it would have passed a different lot's range.

questions.scenarioContext: A staff lunch container is placed in a refrigerator used to hold patient blood specimens. A separate food refrigerator is available outside the specimen area.
questions.prompt: Which correction is appropriate?

choices.A: Remove the food from specimen storage and use the designated food-storage area.
choices.B: Keep the lunch there if its lid is closed.
choices.C: Move the blood tubes into the lunch container to separate them from the food.
choices.D: Keep food on the upper shelf and specimens below it as the sole correction.

questions.explanation: Food should not be stored where blood or other potentially infectious materials are present. A lid or shelf separation does not make the specimen refrigerator an appropriate food-storage location.

questions.scenarioContext: A stable patient's ordered orthostatic measurements are 138/82 mm Hg supine and 116/76 mm Hg standing. The supplied reporting rule flags a systolic fall of at least 20 mm Hg or a diastolic fall of at least 10 mm Hg.
questions.prompt: Which finding meets the stated reporting rule?

choices.A: Neither pressure change, because the rule requires symptoms.
choices.B: Only the 6 mm Hg diastolic fall meets the rule.
choices.C: Neither pressure change, because both threshold limits must be met together.
choices.D: The 22 mm Hg systolic fall.

questions.explanation: 138 - 116 = 22 mm Hg, meeting the supplied systolic threshold; 82 - 76 = 6 mm Hg does not meet the diastolic threshold. The rule uses either pressure criterion and does not require symptoms.

questions.scenarioContext: Immediately before an authorized medication task, the EHR displays a newly entered allergy alert for the ordered drug. The order predates the alert, and no clinician has reviewed the new information. The patient has not received the dose.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Pause administration and obtain clinician review of the new alert before proceeding.
choices.B: Delete the allergy information so the existing order can proceed.
choices.C: Administer a smaller amount without prescriber clarification.
choices.D: Override the alert because the earlier prescription was signed.

questions.explanation: A new safety alert requires reconciliation with the existing order before administration. An older signed order does not establish that the prescriber considered information entered afterward.

questions.scenarioContext: A responsive adult man suddenly cannot speak or cough effectively after eating. He is standing, the trained assistant can encircle his abdomen, and another staff member has activated emergency response. The assistant follows current 2025 AHA-based clinic training.
questions.prompt: Which intervention sequence is indicated while he remains responsive with severe obstruction?

choices.A: Encourage cough alone despite the described inability to cough effectively.
choices.B: Use abdominal thrusts alone without the back-blow cycles in current training.
choices.C: Use blind finger sweeps before the trained obstruction-response cycles.
choices.D: Alternate five back blows with five abdominal thrusts as trained.

questions.explanation: Current training for this described adult severe-obstruction situation uses alternating back blows and abdominal thrusts. If he becomes unresponsive, the response changes to trained CPR; blind finger sweeps should not be used.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: A specified waived assay requires room operation at 15-30 degrees C. A clinic room measures 35 degrees C before testing, and an appropriate temperature-controlled testing area is available.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Establish the required operating conditions before testing under the assay instructions.
choices.B: Use the out-of-range room because the supplies are unopened.
choices.C: Ignore room temperature if the patient specimen looks normal.
choices.D: Run the assay and adjust results downward to compensate for heat.

questions.explanation: The environment does not meet the supplied operating range. Unopened packaging or specimen appearance does not authorize testing outside the method's stated conditions.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: An ordered pre- and post-medication spirometry protocol requires a baseline before the authorized inhaled medication and a second set 15 minutes afterward. The baseline is complete, and the medication is given at 11:20 a.m. The assistant is trained and authorized for the ordered tasks.
questions.prompt: Which planned second-set time follows the protocol?
questions.explanation: 11:20 a.m. plus the specified 15-minute interval is 11:35 a.m. The baseline and post-medication sets should also retain their separate labels and times rather than be combined.

questions.scenarioContext: A comfortable patient cannot keep the mouth closed because of persistent mouth breathing. The oral thermometer instructions require a closed mouth. Clinic protocol permits an available temporal device when oral technique cannot be completed.
questions.prompt: Which approach follows these instructions?

choices.A: Use the permitted temporal device and document the actual measurement route.
choices.B: Take an oral reading with the mouth open and label it as standard oral technique.
choices.C: Use the oral value and add a guessed correction for mouth breathing.
choices.D: Ask the patient to stop breathing long enough to obtain a reading.

questions.explanation: The oral technique cannot meet its stated condition, so the permitted alternative is appropriate. The result should retain its actual route rather than be relabeled or mathematically guessed.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: During a pure-tone hearing screen, a patient waits until each tone ends before raising a hand. The approved response instruction is to signal as soon as a tone is heard, even if it is faint.
questions.prompt: Which coaching best matches the procedure?

choices.A: Raise your hand every few seconds whether or not a tone is heard.
choices.B: Signal when you first hear the tone, even if it is faint.
choices.C: Watch the assistant's face and signal whenever the assistant looks up.
choices.D: Wait until each tone has stopped before responding.

questions.explanation: The response should reflect perception of the actual tone at the instructed time. Delayed or patterned responses do not provide the requested screening behavior.

questions.scenarioContext: A provider plans biopsies from two different sites and orders separate specimen containers with distinct source labels. Both specimens belong to the same patient.
questions.prompt: Which preparation preserves the requested source information?

choices.A: Place both tissues together because the patient identifiers match.
choices.B: Use one unlabeled container and expect the laboratory to distinguish sites by appearance.
choices.C: Prepare one source label and duplicate it for both different sites.
choices.D: Prepare separate correctly labeled containers for each source site.

questions.explanation: Separate containers preserve the association between each tissue and its specific source. A shared patient identity does not make different biopsy sites interchangeable.

questions.scenarioContext: An irregular EKG contains 9 QRS complexes in a 6-second recording window. The assistant is asked to estimate the mean ventricular rate from the full window rather than from one variable R-R interval.
questions.prompt: What is the estimated mean rate?

choices.A: 900 beats/min
choices.B: 9 beats/min
choices.C: 54 beats/min
choices.D: 90 beats/min

questions.explanation: 9 beats x 60 seconds/min / 6 seconds = 90 beats/min. The full-window calculation estimates the mean over that interval; the raw count of 9 is not a one-minute rate.

questions.scenarioContext: A trained, authorized assistant is removing skin staples under an order. The supplied remover instruction says to place the lower jaw beneath the staple center and squeeze the handles so the center bends and the ends lift. The lower jaw is positioned correctly.
questions.prompt: Which action follows this device instruction?

choices.A: Squeeze as instructed to bend and lift the staple.
choices.B: Pull straight upward without operating the handles.
choices.C: Cut the skin around the staple with scissors.
choices.D: Rotate the closed staple sideways through the skin.

questions.explanation: The device's specified bending action lifts the staple ends for removal. Simply pulling or rotating a closed staple does not use the remover as instructed and can injure tissue.

questions.scenarioContext: A signed noncontrolled prescription was routed to an old pharmacy. The patient confirms a new pharmacy. Clinic workflow requires an authorized correction that checks the original transmission before rerouting to avoid duplicate active dispensing.
questions.prompt: Which action follows this workflow?

choices.A: Create a second prescription independently without checking the original.
choices.B: Tell both pharmacies to dispense and let the patient choose later.
choices.C: Verify the original transmission and use the authorized correction process before rerouting.
choices.D: Change the dose while entering the new pharmacy so the prescription looks different.

questions.explanation: The routing problem should be corrected without creating uncontrolled duplicate dispensing or changing the clinical order. Checking the original status is part of the explicitly supplied correction process.

questions.scenarioContext: During venipuncture, a fragile vein visibly collapses when a high-vacuum tube is applied, and the same problem occurs with a second tube. The clinic plan calls for stopping safely and selecting its approved lower-vacuum, small-volume method for the next attempt rather than probing or increasing suction.
questions.prompt: Which plan addresses the observed problem?

choices.A: Keep the same method and probe deeper while another high-vacuum tube is applied.
choices.B: Stop safely and use the approved lower-vacuum, small-volume approach under the collection plan.
choices.C: Repeat the same high-vacuum approach without the required alternate-method step.
choices.D: Apply stronger suction to overcome the observed collapse.

questions.explanation: The repeated collapse is linked to the applied collection vacuum rather than one defective tube. The supplied alternate-method plan addresses that mechanism without unnecessary probing or stronger suction.

questions.prompt: What is the usual adult apical pulse listening location when using a stethoscope?

choices.A: Right second intercostal space at the sternal border.
choices.B: Midline just above the suprasternal notch.
choices.C: Left second intercostal space at the sternal border.
choices.D: Left fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line.

questions.explanation: The usual adult cardiac apex is heard at the left fifth intercostal space near the midclavicular line. The upper sternal-border sites correspond to other cardiac listening areas rather than the usual apical pulse location.

questions.scenarioContext: Before a video visit, the clinician needs to see the patient's face clearly. A bright window behind the patient makes the face appear as a dark silhouette, although the connection works.
questions.prompt: Which setup change best addresses the problem?

choices.A: Keep the silhouette and document a completed visible-face assessment.
choices.B: Ask the patient to turn the camera away from the face.
choices.C: Reposition the patient or lighting so light falls onto the face rather than from behind it.
choices.D: Increase audio volume instead of correcting the image.

questions.explanation: Lighting from behind can obscure the area the clinician needs to see. Adjusting the physical lighting or position improves the actual image rather than substituting unrelated connection changes.

questions.scenarioContext: After a contusion, the provider's approved plan specifies a cold pack with a cloth barrier for 10 minutes at the stated interval. The patient plans to place the pack directly on skin for an hour.
questions.prompt: Which reinforcement follows the plan?

choices.A: Use the cloth barrier and the prescribed 10-minute application period.
choices.B: Extend the application to an hour because longer cold is always better.
choices.C: Leave the pack directly on the skin until the area is numb.
choices.D: Replace the cold pack with a heating pad without checking the plan.

questions.explanation: The provider's specified barrier and time limit govern this application. Direct prolonged exposure or an unapproved substitution changes the plan and can injure skin.

questions.scenarioContext: A provider requests a pair of sterile scissors during a minor procedure. The clinic passing technique specifies closed blades directed away from the receiver and presentation of the finger rings to the receiver.
questions.prompt: Which transfer follows this technique?

choices.A: Hold the scissors by the rings and push the open tips into the receiving hand.
choices.B: Pass the closed scissors with the finger rings presented to the provider.
choices.C: Present the open blade tips toward the provider's hand.
choices.D: Set the open scissors against the patient while the provider reaches for them.

questions.explanation: Presenting the rings with closed blades follows the specified controlled transfer. Directing open cutting tips toward the receiver creates an avoidable sharps hazard.

questions.prompt: What processing is appropriate for a reusable blood pressure cuff contacting only intact skin, using compatible manufacturer instructions?

choices.A: Cleaning followed by the compatible low-level disinfection process.
choices.B: Treating the cuff as an implant and requiring an incompatible sterilization cycle.
choices.C: Immersion in an unapproved high-level chemical without checking compatibility.
choices.D: Detergent cleaning alone with no required disinfection.

questions.explanation: A device contacting only intact skin is noncritical and follows the supplied low-level disinfection instructions. Cleaning alone omits disinfection, while an incompatible stronger process is not an appropriate substitute.

questions.scenarioContext: An older adult with marked kyphosis cannot straighten fully against a stadiometer without pain. The clinic protocol requires documenting the limitation and obtaining the clinician's approved alternative when standard standing height is not feasible.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Document the limitation and obtain instructions for the approved alternative measurement.
choices.B: Record the apparent height as a fully standardized standing measurement without a note.
choices.C: Push the shoulders back until the spine is flat against the board.
choices.D: Invent an adjusted height by adding several centimeters.

questions.explanation: The stated protocol protects the patient and preserves the limitation of the measurement. Forcing posture or inventing an adjustment does not establish a valid standard height.

questions.scenarioContext: Two separately authorized vaccines are administered: product A in the left deltoid and product B in the right deltoid. The assistant is completing the administration records.
questions.prompt: Which site documentation preserves the product-to-site relationship?

choices.A: Assign the left deltoid to both products because both are intramuscular.
choices.B: Omit sites because the lot numbers identify where the doses were given.
choices.C: Record only "both arms" as a shared site for both products.
choices.D: Record product A with the left deltoid and product B with the right deltoid.

questions.explanation: Each product should remain linked to its actual administration site. A shared nonspecific phrase or a lot number alone cannot distinguish which injection occurred in which arm.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient says, "I have not felt feverish." The assistant then measures a temperature of 38.9 degrees C using correct technique. The provider will evaluate the patient.
questions.prompt: How should the assistant document these observations?

choices.A: Change the patient's words to "reports fever" so both entries agree.
choices.B: Record the patient's report and the measured temperature separately, and report the finding as required.
choices.C: Diagnose the cause of the temperature from this information alone.
choices.D: Delete the temperature because it conflicts with the patient's report.

questions.explanation: A subjective report and an objective measurement can differ and both should be preserved. Making them agree by deleting or changing information misrepresents what was reported and observed.

questions.scenarioContext: A patient brings prescribed CPAP equipment for a provider-requested setup check. The assistant is trained and authorized to follow the mask-fit instructions but may not change the prescribed pressure. The patient reports an air leak at the mask edge.
questions.prompt: Which action stays within that task?

choices.A: Tell the patient to abandon therapy permanently because any leak makes it unusable.
choices.B: Change the pressure mode without authorization.
choices.C: Increase the prescribed pressure until the leak is harder to notice.
choices.D: Check the mask placement and connections as instructed and refer an unresolved leak to the qualified clinician or supplier.

questions.explanation: The authorized check concerns fit and equipment connections, not a new treatment setting. Persistent problems should be referred rather than addressed by changing prescribed pressure or stopping the treatment plan independently.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: An ordered semen specimen kit instructs collection directly into the supplied container and prohibits ordinary condoms or unapproved lubricant. Before collection, the patient asks to use a standard lubricated condom and transfer the contents later.
questions.prompt: Which instruction follows the kit?

choices.A: Use the ordinary condom because transfer makes the original container irrelevant.
choices.B: Mix the sample with tap water before transfer.
choices.C: Use the supplied collection container and follow the kit's preparation directions.
choices.D: Add lubricant to the supplied container to increase the volume.

questions.explanation: The collection method and materials must match the supplied kit instructions. Transferring afterward does not remove effects of an unapproved collection material.

questions.scenarioContext: During medication history, a patient says a home injection pen is set to "ten clicks." The pen and its instructions are unavailable, and the assistant cannot verify what volume or dose those clicks represent.
questions.prompt: How should the assistant handle this report?

choices.A: Remove the medication from the history because the dose is uncertain.
choices.B: Convert ten clicks to ten units without identifying the device.
choices.C: Document the patient's exact description and flag the unresolved dose for clinician verification.
choices.D: Record ten milliliters because clicks must correspond to volume.

questions.explanation: Click increments are device-specific and cannot be converted without a reliable reference. Preserving the reported wording and identifying the uncertainty supports verification without inventing a dose.

questions.scenarioContext: The laboratory requires an aliquot to retain the original specimen accession and collection time, with the aliquot-preparation time in a separate field. A specimen was collected at 9:00 a.m. and aliquoted at 9:45 a.m.
questions.prompt: Which labeling record follows the requirement?

choices.A: Replace the collection time with 9:45 a.m. and discard the original accession.
choices.B: Retain the original accession and 9:00 a.m. collection time, and record 9:45 a.m. separately as aliquot preparation.
choices.C: Assign an unrelated accession to make the aliquot look like a new collection.
choices.D: Use only the assistant's initials because the parent tube is nearby.

questions.explanation: The aliquot comes from the original collection, so that identity and time remain relevant. Preparation time is additional information and does not reset the specimen's collection history.

questions.scenarioContext: For a designated airborne-precaution room, the posted removal procedure requires keeping the respirator on until after leaving the room and closing the door. The assistant is appropriately protected and is about to exit.
questions.prompt: Which action follows this procedure?

choices.A: Remove the respirator while still beside the patient, then walk out.
choices.B: Exit and close the door before removing the respirator as directed.
choices.C: Hang the respirator inside the room and leave unprotected.
choices.D: Remove it at the doorway before closing the room door.

questions.explanation: The supplied location rule keeps respiratory protection in place through exit and door closure. Removing it earlier does not meet the stated precaution boundary.

questions.scenarioContext: A device's high-level disinfection method requires its internal channel to be completely filled with solution for the full contact time. An air pocket remains in the channel although the outside is submerged. The assistant is trained in the approved method.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do before starting the required exposure timer?

choices.A: Eliminate the air pocket and fill the channel according to instructions, then complete the full exposure.
choices.B: Count full contact from outer immersion even though the channel was not filled.
choices.C: Start exposure timing while the channel still contains the visible air pocket.
choices.D: Leave the air pocket and estimate an unvalidated time extension.

questions.explanation: The air pocket prevents required contact with part of the channel. Completing the instructed filling step before the full exposure addresses that gap rather than guessing a time compensation.

questions.scenarioContext: An injection station is ready except that there is no approved sharps container within the designated point-of-use location. A portable approved container is available. No needle has yet been used.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do before starting?

choices.A: Plan to carry the used needle uncovered across the room.
choices.B: Place and secure the approved sharps container at the required point-of-use location.
choices.C: Leave the used needle on a tray until the station is closed.
choices.D: Use a drinking cup temporarily and sort the sharps later.

questions.explanation: Point-of-use disposal should be prepared before a contaminated sharp is generated. Planning an exposed carry or temporary unapproved container does not provide the required disposal setup.

questions.scenarioContext: A designated instrument load has a clinic release rule requiring a negative biological monitor result before use. Its mechanical readings and chemical indicators are acceptable, but the biological result is still pending.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Keep the load on hold until all specified release conditions are met.
choices.B: Release it because acceptable chemical indicators replace the pending biological condition.
choices.C: Change the pending field to negative to match the other indicators.
choices.D: Use it only for the first patient while the result is pending.

questions.explanation: The clinic rule explicitly includes a completed negative biological result. Favorable other monitors do not complete a still-pending release condition.

questions.scenarioContext: An authorized, trained assistant is preparing a clinically verified non-IV dose of a nonvaccine medication: 600 mg. Each new single-dose vial contains 1.5 mL at 300 mg/mL. The task is to determine the minimum unopened-vial supply needed for this one patient; unused medication will be handled under policy.
questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of vials required?

choices.A: 2 vials
choices.B: 1 vial
choices.C: 4 vials
choices.D: 3 vials

questions.explanation: The dose requires 600 mg / 300 mg/mL = 2 mL. One vial supplies only 1.5 mL, or 450 mg, so the minimum supply is two new vials; more vials are unnecessary for this dose.

questions.scenarioContext: After a multi-tube draw, the assistant realizes the laboratory's required order of draw was not followed. The tubes are identified correctly, but the lab procedure requires reporting the actual sequence so acceptability can be determined for the ordered tests.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Rewrite the collection record to show the intended sequence.
choices.B: Assume the error cannot matter and conceal it from the laboratory.
choices.C: Open the tubes and exchange their contents to recreate the required order.
choices.D: Report the actual collection sequence and follow laboratory guidance on specimen acceptability.

questions.explanation: The laboratory needs the actual preanalytical information to evaluate the affected tests. Rewriting history or transferring contents does not reverse a possible additive-carryover problem.

questions.scenarioContext: A provider-approved instruction for an ordered metered-dose inhaler with spacer says to release one puff into the spacer and inhale it as directed before the next puff. The patient plans to release all prescribed puffs into the spacer together.
questions.prompt: Which reinforcement matches the supplied technique?

choices.A: Double the number of puffs to compensate for releasing them together.
choices.B: Release every puff together and leave them in the chamber until later.
choices.C: Remove the spacer and spray toward the cheek instead of using the ordered method.
choices.D: Release and inhale one puff at a time, following the prescribed interval and technique.

questions.explanation: The supplied method uses a separate inhalation for each released puff. Combining puffs or independently increasing the dose does not follow the prescribed delivery technique.

questions.scenarioContext: At ambulatory-monitor return, staff verify that the recorder clock ran one hour behind the correct clinic time. The patient's diary used the correct time. Raw recordings and diary entries are available for review.
questions.prompt: Which handling supports accurate event correlation?

choices.A: Silently rewrite the patient's diary to hide the discrepancy.
choices.B: Preserve the originals and flag the verified clock offset for the reviewer.
choices.C: Assume every diary symptom is false because the clocks differ.
choices.D: Delete the recordings made during diary-reported events.

questions.explanation: A known clock offset is relevant to correlating events and should be made explicit. Preserving the original data allows an authorized reviewer to account for it without concealed changes.

questions.scenarioContext: A provider orders compression stockings after confirming suitability. The fitting guide requires both ankle and calf measurements to fall within one size. Medium accepts ankle 22-26 cm and calf 34-40 cm; large accepts ankle 26-30 cm and calf 40-46 cm. The patient measures 24 cm at the ankle and 44 cm at the calf.
questions.prompt: Which fitting decision follows the guide?

choices.A: Choose medium and roll the upper band tightly to compensate.
choices.B: Obtain approved fitting guidance because neither available size matches both measurements.
choices.C: Select medium based only on the ankle measurement.
choices.D: Select large based only on the calf measurement.

questions.explanation: The ankle matches medium, but the calf exceeds its range; large fits the calf but not the ankle. The supplied rule requires both measurements, so an authorized alternative fitting is needed rather than a one-measurement choice.

questions.scenarioContext: A prescribed nasal-spray device is new. Its instructions require two test actuations away from the patient before the first administered dose. The trained, authorized assistant has not yet primed it.
questions.prompt: Which preparation follows the device instructions?

choices.A: Count the two test actuations as the patient's administered dose.
choices.B: Complete the two directed test actuations away from the patient before the dose.
choices.C: Skip the first-use prime because the package was unopened.
choices.D: Prime toward the patient's nose and count any uncertain spray as administration.

questions.explanation: The specified priming step prepares the device before delivery of the ordered dose. Test sprays away from the patient are not patient administration and should not be counted as such.

questions.scenarioContext: For a specific capillary microcollection, the laboratory guide lists EDTA before serum and warns staff not to substitute the venous tube sequence. A coworker plans to collect serum first by habit.
questions.prompt: Which action follows this collection-specific instruction?

choices.A: Label both specimens as venous to justify the planned sequence.
choices.B: Pour part of the serum specimen into the EDTA container afterward.
choices.C: Use the venous sequence regardless of specimen method.
choices.D: Use the stated capillary sequence, with EDTA before serum.

questions.explanation: The guide explicitly distinguishes its capillary sequence from venous collection. Following a different method's habit or transferring blood afterward does not meet the stated microcollection process.

questions.scenarioContext: A child can use the clinic's approved faces pain scale but asks whether to choose the face that looks happiest. The scale instructions say to select the face representing how much the child hurts, not mood.
questions.prompt: Which explanation best supports valid self-report?

choices.A: Let the assistant choose based on how much you are crying.
choices.B: Choose the face that shows how much you hurt, even if your mood is different.
choices.C: Choose the middle face so the result is easier to compare.
choices.D: Choose the happiest face whenever you feel cheerful.

questions.explanation: The supplied scale asks the child to report pain intensity rather than happiness or sadness. An observer-selected face or a default middle response replaces the child's actual self-report.

questions.scenarioContext: The clinic limits an assistant to two unsuccessful venipuncture attempts on one patient before contacting the designated lead for further collection arrangements. Two attempts have failed, and the patient remains stable.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do next?

choices.A: Make a third attempt with a fresh needle without contacting the designated lead.
choices.B: Ask an unapproved helper to continue attempts outside the clinic process.
choices.C: Stop further attempts and contact the designated lead under the policy.
choices.D: Continue probing through the second puncture instead of treating it as unsuccessful.

questions.explanation: The attempt limit has been reached and applies despite use of fresh equipment. Escalating through the defined process avoids unauthorized repeated attempts or probing.

questions.scenarioContext: A calm child will receive an ordered injection while seated on a caregiver's lap. The clinic's trained comfort-hold method supports the child and keeps the injection limb steady without restricting breathing. The assistant and caregiver have been instructed in it.
questions.prompt: Which preparation follows this method?

choices.A: Allow the injection limb to swing freely while the needle is inserted.
choices.B: Ask an untrained bystander to force the child flat without using the approved method.
choices.C: Use the trained supportive hold and pause for help if a safe steady position cannot be maintained.
choices.D: Press the child's face into the caregiver's chest to prevent movement.

questions.explanation: The described method supports safe positioning without restricting breathing. Uncontrolled limb movement or improvised force is not equivalent to the trained comfort hold.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: A test's supplied waived-method instructions accept capillary whole blood only. The clinic receives a tube of venous plasma, and no authorized alternative method is available in the clinic.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Run the plasma under the capillary method because both originated from blood.
choices.B: Obtain instructions for an acceptable specimen or appropriately authorized laboratory route without modifying the waived method.
choices.C: Relabel the plasma as capillary whole blood.
choices.D: Mix the plasma with water to approximate the specified specimen.

questions.explanation: The supplied specimen requirement is part of the test method. A different blood fraction cannot be treated as equivalent or made acceptable by relabeling or unvalidated modification.

questions.scenarioContext: Before a provider-performed procedure involving sedation, the clinic checklist requires confirmation of a responsible adult escort before sedating medication is given. The patient says no escort is available and plans to drive home. The assistant cannot waive this requirement.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Treat the patient's access to a car as an escort substitute.
choices.B: Flag the unmet requirement and obtain the procedural clinician's direction before sedation proceeds.
choices.C: Start the planned sequence and ask about an escort only after sedation.
choices.D: Independently promise discharge without an escort if the patient later feels alert.

questions.explanation: The stated prerequisite is not met and needs clinician resolution before sedation. The assistant should not invent an exception or treat access to a car as an appropriate escort.

questions.scenarioContext: A drug-level collection order specifies a specimen exactly 2 hours after an observed oral dose. The documented dose time is 8:40 a.m. No other timing condition applies.
questions.prompt: At what time should the specimen be scheduled?
questions.explanation: 8:40 a.m. plus 2 hours is 10:40 a.m. Collection timing should be based on the actual documented dose time, not the start of the clinic day.

questions.scenarioContext: A trained, authorized assistant has a clinically verified order for 125 mg of an oral liquid. Its verified label states 5% weight/volume, defined on the label as 5 g per 100 mL. Use 1 g = 1,000 mg.
questions.prompt: What volume provides the ordered amount?

choices.A: 25 mL
choices.C: 2.5 mL

questions.explanation: 5 g per 100 mL = 5,000 mg per 100 mL = 50 mg/mL. 125 mg / 50 mg/mL = 2.5 mL; treating the percentage as 5 mg/mL would give a tenfold larger volume.

questions.scenarioContext: A processed specimen appears lipemic. The test-specific laboratory instruction says to submit it with the observed appearance documented; laboratory staff will evaluate assay-specific acceptability. The assistant is not authorized to reject it solely by appearance.
questions.prompt: Which action follows the instruction?

choices.A: Discard the specimen automatically because every lipemic sample is unusable.
choices.B: Tell the patient to stop medication and repeat it without an order.
choices.C: Document the appearance and submit it for the specified laboratory evaluation.
choices.D: Dilute the specimen with water to make it clear before submission.

questions.explanation: The supplied instruction assigns acceptability review to the laboratory for this assay. Appearance should be reported rather than used for an unauthorized blanket rejection or specimen modification.

questions.scenarioContext: A disinfecting chemical's safety data sheet requires a specified chemical-resistant glove for the task and states that ordinary thin examination gloves are unsuitable. The required gloves are available.
questions.prompt: Which glove choice follows the safety data sheet?

choices.A: Two pairs of the unsuitable examination gloves without approval.
choices.B: The specified chemical-resistant gloves.
choices.C: Ordinary examination gloves because all medical gloves resist all chemicals.
choices.D: Bare hands for a shorter exposure time.

questions.explanation: The protection must match the chemical's stated compatibility requirement. Doubling an unsuitable material or shortening unprotected exposure does not establish the specified chemical barrier.

questions.scenarioContext: An assistant removes the protective cap from a new medication vial before an authorized injection. The clinic preparation instruction requires cleaning the rubber stopper before needle entry, including on newly opened vials.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do before entry?

choices.A: Skip preparation because the protective cap guarantees a sterile stopper.
choices.B: Clean the stopper using the instructed aseptic preparation.
choices.C: Touch the stopper with a fingertip to confirm it is dry and clean.
choices.D: Remove the entire stopper and pour the medication into the syringe.

questions.explanation: A protective vial cap is not a guarantee that the stopper needs no preparation. The supplied aseptic step still applies before needle entry.

questions.scenarioContext: A completed packaged sterilizer load is still hot. The validated handling instructions require full cooling in the designated clean area before handling and storage.
questions.prompt: Which action follows the instructions?

choices.A: Stack the hot packages tightly on a cold wet counter to cool them faster.
choices.B: Allow the packages to cool fully in the designated area before handling them for storage.
choices.C: Handle the hot packs with damp towels and return them to stock.
choices.D: Open each hot package so the instruments cool directly in the room air.

questions.explanation: The stated cooling step is part of safe post-cycle handling. Improvised wet cooling, tight stacking, or opening sterile barriers does not follow the validated handling process.

questions.prompt: Which instrument provides a vibrating stimulus during a sensory examination?

choices.A: The tuning fork.
choices.B: The reflex hammer.
choices.C: The tongue depressor.
choices.D: The otoscope.

questions.explanation: A tuning fork provides a vibrating stimulus for the requested examination. A reflex hammer is intended to elicit reflexes and does not replace that stimulus.

questions.scenarioContext: An assistant performed ordered wound care at 10:00 a.m. An urgent interruption delayed documentation until 1:15 p.m. The EHR retains the current entry timestamp and allows the actual service time to be recorded.
questions.prompt: Which documentation is appropriate?

choices.A: Leave the care undocumented because the original time has passed.
choices.B: Change the system timestamp so it appears the note was entered at 10:00 a.m.
choices.C: Enter the care now, retain the entry timestamp, and identify 10:00 a.m. as the actual service time.
choices.D: Record the wound care as occurring at 1:15 p.m. even though that was only the entry time.

questions.explanation: A late entry should distinguish when care occurred from when documentation was entered. Preserving both times maintains an accurate sequence without altering the audit record.

questions.scenarioContext: A capillary hemoglobin collection device has a visible air bubble in its optical filling area. Its instructions require a complete continuous fill without bubbles and prohibit topping up a partially filled device.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Ignore the bubble because the patient's name is correct.
choices.B: Add a second drop to the partially filled device despite the prohibition.
choices.C: Tap the device aggressively until the sample splashes from the filling area.
choices.D: Use a new device and obtain a proper continuous fill under the instructions.

questions.explanation: The visible bubble fails the supplied filling criterion. A fresh correctly filled device follows the method, whereas prohibited topping up or rough handling does not validate the sample.

questions.scenarioContext: During EKG acquisition, the displayed tracing becomes flat. The assistant immediately checks the patient, who is awake, speaking, and has a palpable pulse. The clinic recording procedure calls for checking connections and escalating unresolved recording faults in this situation.
questions.prompt: Which action follows that assessment?

choices.A: Begin chest compressions from the display alone despite the confirmed responsive patient.
choices.B: Record cardiac arrest as established while disregarding the patient assessment.
choices.C: Check the recording connections and follow the unresolved-fault process if needed.
choices.D: Delay checking the connections and assign a rhythm diagnosis from the flat display alone.

questions.explanation: The patient findings do not match a cardiac-arrest conclusion based only on the display. After the immediate patient check, the stated recording-fault process is appropriate rather than treating an unverified device display as a diagnosis.

questions.scenarioContext: After wound evaluation, a provider orders removal of alternate sutures only, leaving the others until reassessment. The sutures are clearly identified, and the trained, authorized assistant sees no new wound problem.
questions.prompt: Which implementation follows the order?

choices.A: Change the planned reassessment interval independently after removal.
choices.B: Remove only the specified alternate sutures and leave the remainder for the ordered reassessment.
choices.C: Remove only the knots while leaving unidentified fragments in the tissue.
choices.D: Remove every suture because the wound appears closed.

questions.explanation: The order limits today's removal to a defined subset. A closed appearance does not authorize removal of the remaining sutures or a change in the follow-up plan.

questions.scenarioContext: An assistant develops vomiting and diarrhea before a patient-care shift. The clinic staff-health procedure requires immediate reporting and occupational-health direction before patient contact for these symptoms.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Use a mask as an independent substitute for the staff-health review.
choices.B: Begin patient contact and report only if several patients become ill.
choices.C: Hide the symptoms because no diagnosis has been made.
choices.D: Report the symptoms and follow staff-health direction before patient-care work.

questions.explanation: The symptom-based staff-health rule applies before a diagnosis is known. The assistant should not substitute self-selected precautions for the required work-fitness review.

questions.category: Point of Care Testing and Laboratory Procedures
questions.scenarioContext: A laboratory calls with an authenticated amendment: a previously released potassium result of 5.9 mmol/L is corrected to 4.2 mmol/L. The ordering clinician already received the earlier report. Clinic procedure requires promptly relaying authenticated amendments and documenting the correction and notification.
questions.prompt: What should the assistant do?

choices.A: Notify the patient of a treatment change chosen by the assistant.
choices.B: Preserve only the first value and ignore the authenticated correction.
choices.C: Relay the authenticated corrected result promptly and document it through the approved amendment workflow.
choices.D: Enter the amendment silently without the required active notification.

questions.explanation: The clinician may still be acting on the superseded information, so the supplied active notification process matters. The assistant records the amendment without independently selecting a treatment change.

questions.prompt: How many surface electrodes are used for a standard resting 12-lead EKG?

choices.A: 12 electrodes
choices.B: 6 electrodes
choices.C: 4 electrodes
choices.D: 10 electrodes

questions.explanation: Four limb electrodes plus six precordial electrodes total ten physical electrodes. The number of derived leads is different from the count of electrodes attached to the patient.

questions.scenarioContext: A provider orders two different vaccine products as separate injections. They are not a licensed combination, and the instructions do not authorize mixing. The assistant is trained and authorized for the ordered injections.
questions.prompt: Which preparation follows the orders?

choices.A: Prepare each product separately in its own labeled syringe.
choices.B: Administer only the combined volume of whichever product is easier to draw.
choices.C: Mix the products in one syringe to reduce the number of punctures.
choices.D: Transfer one prepared vaccine into the other syringe without checking compatibility.

questions.explanation: Separately ordered products should remain separate when there is no licensed or instructed combination. The assistant must not create a combination vaccine by mixing products to reduce injections.

questions.scenarioContext: A blood ethanol collection kit specifies the supplied nonalcohol skin preparation for this assay. The assistant also has routine alcohol pads. All other kit requirements are met.
questions.prompt: Which preparation should be selected?

choices.A: A routine alcohol pad instead of the specified kit preparation.
choices.B: The supplied nonalcohol skin preparation specified for the ethanol specimen.
choices.C: Any scented cleanser because only the tube additive matters.
choices.D: An alcohol pad followed by a label saying nonalcohol preparation.
